Revised assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:

- Policy stance: The FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 0–1/4 percent with strong forward guidance and continued sizable purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS/CMBS, alongside repo and ON RRP operations. IOER at 0.10% and the primary credit rate at 0.25% support highly accommodative financial conditions and smooth market functioning.

- Beige Book signals: District reports indicate a partial rebound from the spring trough—consumer spending and vehicle sales improved as nonessential businesses reopened; manufacturing activity increased; and housing/refinance demand strengthened on low rates. However, conditions remain well below pre-pandemic levels, with notable weakness in commercial real estate and the energy sector, and high uncertainty tied to the virus path.

- Credit conditions (SLOOS): Banks broadly tightened standards across C&I, CRE, and consumer loans, with softer loan demand from businesses. Despite strong mortgage/refi activity, most mortgage categories saw tighter standards. This bank credit tightening risks muting the pass-through of easier financial conditions to the real economy.

- Outlook: Policy is appropriately supportive and has improved market functioning, but Beige Book and SLOOS together point to an uneven recovery with considerable downside risks. The observed rebound warrants a modestly less negative tone than a SLOOS-only read, yet overall conditions remain fragile.
